purpose: personal account of applying CRISP-DM as a reference framework to AI engineering work

required_facts.fact: CRISP-DM was developed in the 1990s for structuring data projects and was later adopted by the data science and machine learning community.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 1: framework origin and adoption are stated.

required_facts.fact: Modern AI engineering uses LLM APIs, retrieval pipelines, agents, prompts, evaluation tools, and production observability.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 3-5: changed stack and continuing process structure are described.

required_facts.fact: The six CRISP-DM phases are Business Understanding, Data Understanding, Data Preparation, Modeling, Evaluation, and Deployment.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 10-20: six phases are listed.

required_facts.fact: The example is an online classifieds listing feature that suggests title, description, category, and price from a user-uploaded photo.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 22-29: classifieds scenario is introduced.

required_facts.fact: Business Understanding defines success, such as reducing listing time from five minutes to one and abandonment from 15 percent to 5 percent.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 32-38: business objectives and AI-versus-simple-solution decision are described.

required_facts.fact: Data Understanding examines image storage, formats, resolutions, frequency of images, and blurry, rotated, or incomplete inputs.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 40-51: data questions and related listing fields are listed.

required_facts.fact: Data Preparation can validate formats, normalize image size or orientation, prepare metadata, and define structured outputs.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 53-64: preparation tasks and RAG equivalents are described.

required_facts.fact: Modeling in a foundation-model system includes prompt design, output schema, validation, and tests for image extraction reliability.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 66-81: modeling shift, components, and iteration are stated.

required_facts.fact: Evaluation may compare current and AI-assisted workflows with an A/B test against the original goals.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 83-94: evaluation metrics and return to earlier phases are described.

required_facts.fact: Deployment integrates the service, handles errors and unexpected inputs, monitors performance, and can send production findings back to earlier phases.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 96-114: deployment responsibilities and iterative lifecycle are stated.

author_attribution: Attribute the CRISP-DM comparison and classifieds example to the source author; preserve that it is a reference structure rather than a claim that AI engineering is identical to traditional ML.
